$comment: Term base. The vocabulary a translation must not reinvent — derived from the 1,449 Spanish strings that already shipped, so a new pass agrees with the old one instead of introducing a second word for the same thing. Add a row when a term first appears; a reviewer reads this before the catalog.

register.$note: Informal throughout — measured on the existing translations, 166 tú-forms against 27 usted. A fitness app addresses the person training, not a customer. French is the opposite: vous throughout, measured at 118 vous-forms against 62 tu. Do not assume one register carries across languages. German is du as well — measured at 122 du-forms against 7 genuine Sie ones, which were corrected. Note that capitalised Sie/Ihr is ambiguous in German (formal you, but also she/they/her), so those seven were read by hand rather than counted.

doNotTranslate.$note: Product and brand nouns. Kept in English by the existing translations, so keep them.

es.$regimenNote: Changed from 'Régimen' to 'Programa' on 2026-08-15 (kegan's call). Two reasons. 'Rutina' was translating BOTH Regimen (29 keys) and Routine (8), so the app's two distinct objects were the same word in Spanish; and 'Régimen' reads dietary or clinical to a Spanish speaker — régimen alimenticio — which is wrong for a training program. 'Programa' mirrors what French already does (Programme/Routine) and leaves 'Rutina' to mean Routine only. 47 keys converted, with gender agreement: el programa, este programa, ¡Programa creado!, Nombre del programa.
es.$addedNote: Session, Elite and Rival were added 2026-08-16 after `npm run i18n:review` flagged them as recurring product nouns with no row — the growth rule working as intended rather than a collision found the hard way.

fr.$streakNote: RESOLVED 2026-08-15 (kegan asked for it explicitly, having first chosen to leave it open). 'Série' had translated BOTH Streak (60 keys) and Set (68) — one word for two unrelated things across 128 user-facing strings. 'Série' is the standard French term for a training set and could not move, so Streak took a new word: 'Flamme'. Chosen on the app's OWN iconography rather than on taste — src/components/StreakFlame.jsx, 82 Flame references across components/pages, and 8 French strings already carrying 🔥. So the word now matches the icon the user is looking at, and it is feminine like 'Série', which means every article and agreement carried over untouched. Rejected: 'Suite' (ambiguous — 'la suite' is also 'the rest', and it appears in UI as 'voir la suite'), 'Régularité' and 'Assiduité' (abstract, cannot be counted or saved), 'Chaîne' (works for the don't-break-the-chain idiom but fights the flame iconography the app already ships). French idiom was used where a literal swap was worse: the flame is lit ('s'allume'), kept alive ('entretenir la flamme', 'garder votre flamme allumée') and goes out ('s'éteint à minuit'). NOT a native sign-off — see _meta.json $passes.
fr.$setNote: TWO STRINGS DELIBERATELY STILL SAY 'série' FOR A SET, and they are the ones that made the collision visible: onboarding.first_workout.body ('Deux minutes. Une seule série. La flamme s'allume aujourd'hui.') and progress.slide.streak.tipNone ('Une seule série compte … et la flamme démarre à 1.'). Each used ONE word for BOTH senses in adjacent sentences. A find-and-replace over this term corrupts them — check these two by hand before any future sweep.
fr.$addedNote: Session, Elite and Rival were added 2026-08-16 after `npm run i18n:review` flagged them as recurring product nouns with no row — the growth rule working as intended rather than a collision found the hard way.

pt.$note: pt-BR, not pt-PT — measured on the 1,486 strings that already shipped: 99 Brazilian markers (Compartilhar, Salvar, Excluir, Configurações, registrar, -ndo gerunds) against 6 European ones, and zero 'vós'. Register carries NO explicit pronoun: você-form imperatives (Acompanhe, Registre, Abra) with seu/sua possessives, which is standard Brazilian UI voice. Derived 2026-08-16 before the coverage pass, so 2,310 new strings agree with the 1,486 old ones instead of inventing second words.
pt.$streakNote: No collision here, unlike French: Streak is Sequência and Set is Série, two different words. Do not 'simplify' Streak to Série.
pt.$gymNote: 'Academia', never 'ginásio' — in Brazil a ginásio is a sports hall, not a fitness gym. The shipped strings were split 2/3 and the three ginásio ones were corrected in the same commit, with the gender change they force (ao ginásio → à academia, seu → sua).
pt.$regimenNote: Already the majority in the shipped strings (Programa 2, Plano 1) and it agrees with both other released Romance locales — es Programa, fr Programme — so Rotina is free to mean Routine.
pt.$addedNote: Session, Elite and Rival were added 2026-08-16 after `npm run i18n:review` flagged them as recurring product nouns with no row — the growth rule working as intended rather than a collision found the hard way.

de.$note: Derived 2026-08-16 from the 1,486 strings that already shipped, before the coverage pass, so 2,310 new strings agree with the old ones. Register is du throughout. German runs about 15% longer than English here (measured over 954 comparable strings) — less than the 30% rule of thumb, but check the pinned-CTA onboarding screens with the pseudolocale before releasing.
de.$workoutNote: Was split Training 66 / Workout 16 in the shipped strings. Both are idiomatic German, but a glossary exists so new copy does not add a third rendering — the majority wins and the 16 were converted. Compounds follow it too: Workout-Daten → Trainingsdaten.
de.$streakNote: No collision, unlike French: Streak is Serie and Set is Satz. Measured — 'Serie' is used for Set zero times. Do not let a future pass render Set as Serie.
de.$coinNote: Flexyn's soft currency. Every locale translates the plain noun and keeps the brand name 'Flex Coins' in English (buyConfirmDialog.flexCoins). German was split Münzen 14 / Coins 4 — the four were gift.* and were converted to the majority, which also agrees with es/fr/pt.
de.$regimenNote: Was rendered THREE ways in the shipped strings — Plan 15, Trainingsplan 7, Programm 7 — and 'Plan' also translated the English word Plan (5 keys), so one German word served two different objects. Settled on Programm, which agrees with every other Romance/Latin locale here (es Programa, fr Programme, pt Programa) and frees Plan to mean Plan. 32 keys converted, with the gender change it forces: der Plan is masculine, das Programm is neuter — deinen ersten Trainingsplan → dein erstes Programm.
de.$addedNote: Session, Elite and Rival were added 2026-08-16 after `npm run i18n:review` flagged them as recurring product nouns with no row — the growth rule working as intended rather than a collision found the hard way.

it.$note: Derived 2026-08-16 from the 1,482 strings that already shipped, before the coverage pass, so the new strings agree with the old ones. Register is tu throughout — measured at 128 tu-forms against 2 apparent Lei ones, and both of those were false positives ("i suoi progressi" of a goal, "le sue statistiche" of a rival), the same ambiguity German has with Sie. 87 tu-imperatives against 0 Lei-imperatives confirms it. Italian runs a little longer than English here; check the pinned-CTA onboarding screens with the pseudolocale before releasing.
it.$setNote: Set and Sets share one form because Italian "serie" is invariant in the plural (la serie / le serie) — es, fr, pt and de all inflect theirs, so Italian is the first locale here to need the exemption. This is one term with an invariant plural, NOT the one-word-two-jobs defect; that one was Streak, and it is recorded above.
it.$streakNote: RESOLVED 2026-08-16, and it is the French defect in a second locale: "Serie" translated BOTH Streak (20 keys) and Set (30) — one word for two unrelated things. "Serie" is the standard Italian term for a training set and could not move, so Streak took a new word. Chosen the same way French chose Flamme: from the app's OWN iconography rather than taste — StreakFlame.jsx exists, 82 Flame references across components, and three Italian strings already carried 🔥. "Fiamma" is feminine like "Serie", so every article and agreement carried over untouched. Italian was luckier than French: no string carried both senses at once, so none needed hand-unpicking — but the idiom still does not survive a find-and-replace, because an Italian flame is accesa, tenuta viva, and si spegne. Set stays Serie; do not let a future pass render Streak as Serie again.
it.$rivalNote: The two shipped Rival strings rendered it "Nemesi", but English uses "nemesis" as a SEPARATE word in onboarding.enable_push.body and pushOptIn.subtitle — every other locale translates that one on its own (némesis / némésis). Leaving Nemesi on Rival would have handed Italian one word for two English terms across the whole Gym Rival feature, so the two were converted to Rivale while it cost two strings instead of ten.
it.$capsuleNote: Capsule is doNotTranslate and the corpus already agreed 10 to 3; the three lowercase "capsula/capsule" strings were converted to the majority, the same outlier German had with its single "Kapsel".

nl.$note: Derived 2026-08-16 from the 1,457 strings that already shipped, before the coverage pass. Register is je throughout — measured at 177 je-forms and 45 je-imperatives against 0 u-imperatives. Dutch closes its compounds, so a kept term hides inside a longer word (welkomstcapsule, trainingsschema); i18n-review handles that, do not "fix" it.
nl.$registerNote: The French two-registers defect, third locale: SIX strings were in the formal u register inside a je catalog, and all six sat in cardio.* — "Waar gaat u fietsen?", "Voer uw statistieken in", "Hoe wilt u het loggen?". A pronoun count alone nearly missed them, because bare "u" is also the Dutch abbreviation for uur; six of the twelve hits were the unit. Read them, do not count them.
nl.$workoutNote: Was split Training 48 / workout 13 in the shipped strings. The majority won and the 13 were converted, which is the same call German made.
nl.$streakNote: No collision, unlike French and Italian: Streak is Reeks and Set stays the English Set, so the two never met. Do not let a future pass render Set as Reeks.
nl.$regimenNote: Dutch is the ONE locale here that does not use the Programa/Programme/Programma/Programm family, and it diverges on measured evidence rather than by accident. The shipped strings were split Schema 22 / Programma 10, so the majority won. The reason German needed Programm does not transfer: German "Plan" was already translating the English word Plan, whereas Dutch renders Plan as plan/plannen everywhere (trainingsplan, maaltijdplannen) and never as Schema — so Schema was free, and it is also the ordinary Dutch word for a training programme. The 10 Programma strings were converted. One string had Schema doing two jobs at once — regimens.templateStoreDesc rendered "workout templates" as trainingsschema's — and it is now trainingssjablonen, which agrees with regimens.toast.copied.

pl.$note: Derived 2026-08-16 from the 1,457 strings that already shipped, before the coverage pass. Register is ty throughout — 63 ty-forms against 0 Pan/Pani ones, the cleanest register measurement of any locale here. Polish inflects for case, so a kept term appears as seria/serii/serie/serię and a glossary row will not match on the nominative alone; i18n-review handles that, do not "fix" it.
pl.$streakNote: RESOLVED 2026-08-16, and it is the French defect in a THIRD locale: "seria" carried both Set (29 strings) and Streak (18). Seria is the standard Polish word for a training set and could not move, so Streak took a new one. Polish deliberately does NOT follow the Flamme/Fiamma flame choice, and the reason is grammatical rather than aesthetic: the Polish flame word "płomień" is MASCULINE while "seria" is feminine, so it would have forced an agreement change on all 18 strings for nothing, whereas "passa" is feminine — every article and adjective carried over untouched, exactly the property that made Flamme work in French. Passa is also the ordinary Polish word for a run of this kind (dobra passa), it is countable and saveable, which is what a streak has to be, and it does not fight the 🔥 the three notification titles already carry. All 18 were written by hand; the term change moves the verb too — a passa is utrzymywana and it kończy się.
pl.$nutritionNote: Was split Odżywianie 4 / Żywienie 2; the majority won and the two were converted.
pl.$regimenNote: The German defect, second locale, and settled the same way. "Plan" carried both Regimen (26 strings) AND the English word Plan (11) — one Polish word for two different objects, which is precisely what forced German off Plan and onto Programm. Program was already the rendering in 7 shipped strings, so the minority was promoted rather than a new word invented, and it converges with es Programa, fr Programme, pt Programa and de Programm. The 26 were rewritten by hand because Polish declines: plan → program, planu → programu, planów → programów, Architekt Planów → Architekt Programów. Dutch is the one locale that stays off this family, and for a reason that does not apply here — Dutch Plan was never ambiguous.

$growthRule: STANDING RULE (kegan, 2026-08-16): when the app gains a new product noun, add a row here for EVERY released locale in the same change that ships it — not later. This file is the only thing stopping a term from acquiring a second and third translation, and every collision found so far was a noun that grew into the app without a row: Regimen had THREE German renderings while 'Plan' also meant Plan; Spanish 'Rutina' served Regimen and Routine; French 'Série' served Streak and Set across 128 strings. Unpicking one afterwards is expensive — the French fix needed 15 hand-written strings, because a find-and-replace corrupts the sentences that carry both senses. `npm run i18n:review` lists recurring mid-sentence-capitalised nouns with no row here, so the rule is checked rather than remembered.
